title: Forms, fields, labels and native validation

videos.script: Most of a page only speaks. A form is the part that listens. {{form}} The bookshop wants people to order books from its site. Name, email, the title they want, how many copies. Four boxes and a button. {{send}} When somebody presses that button, the browser does something precise. It walks through the form, takes every field that has a name and a value, and writes them into a request. That request is all the server ever gets. {{label}} Before any of that, somebody has to know what each box is for. A word printed next to a box is not enough. It has to be joined to the box, so that a screen reader can say it, and so that clicking the word puts the cursor in the field. {{types}} Then there are the kinds of field. An email address, a phone number, a date, a choice between two formats. Each has its own element or type, and each brings a different keyboard on a phone. {{check}} The browser can also check the answers before anything is sent. A required field left empty. An email with nothing after the at sign. A number outside its range. It stops the request and says what is wrong. {{server}} And then the lesson's last point, the one that matters most for safety. Those checks run in the reader's browser. The reader can switch them off. So the server checks everything again, every time. {{end}}
